# Analyzing NBA Recruits

This analysis explores whether being a top-ranked high school basketball recruit predicts a future NBA career.

```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

## Exploring the NBA Recruits Data

```{r}
nba_recruits <- read_excel("data/nba_recruits.xlsx")

glimpse(nba_recruits)

head(nba_recruits)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r}
nba_recruits |>
  select(rank, nba_mean_ws48, top_mean_wa, total_seasons, drafted) |>
  summary()
```

## Creating Ordered Factors

```{r}
#| cache: true

basketball_tibble <- nba_recruits |>
  mutate(
    tier = factor(
      tier,
      levels = c(
        "Never played",
        "Brief career",
        "Solid career",
        "All-Star level",
        "Superstar"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    recruit_group = factor(
      recruit_group,
      levels = c(
        "#1–10",
        "#11–25",
        "#26–50",
        "#51–100",
        "Outside top 100"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

## Recruiting Rank vs. Peak NBA Performance

This scatter plot explores whether highly ranked high school basketball recruits achieve greater peak NBA performance.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| warning: false

plot_data <- basketball_tibble |>
  filter(!is.na(rank), !is.na(top_mean_wa))

notable_players <- plot_data |>
  arrange(desc(top_mean_wa)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = rank, y = top_mean_wa)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = tier), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = notable_players,
    aes(label = name),
    vjust = -0.8,
    size = 3.5,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Does Recruiting Rank Predict NBA Success?",
    subtitle = "High school recruiting rank vs. peak NBA Wins Added",
    x = "High School Recruiting Rank",
    y = "Peak NBA Wins Added",
    color = "NBA Career Tier"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
